blocks.text: 1. Advanced RAG
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719519-735008123.png

Naive RAG established the four stage baseline and named where it breaks down. Advanced RAG, the general shift toward added correction stages, names the overall strategy this entire module explores one technique at a time.
It inserts pre-retrieval and post-retrieval steps around that same core pipeline.
2. Pre-Retrieval Versus Post-Retrieval
Advanced RAG techniques fall into two broad groups: pre-retrieval steps that improve the query before searching, and post-retrieval steps that improve the retrieved chunks before generation.
Both groups wrap around the same core retrieve then generate pipeline established in Naive RAG.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Stage type","What it improves"],"rows":[["Pre-retrieval","The query before it is used to search"],["Post-retrieval","The retrieved chunks before they reach the model"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Improving The Query Before Searching
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719520-93337911.png
A rewritten or expanded query, the technique covered as query rewriting and query expansion in Retrieval, retrieves better matching chunks.
This fixes the search itself rather than compensating for it later.
4. Improving The Chunks Before Generating
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719520-610824968.png
Re-ranking or filtering retrieved chunks, the same top-k selection and context compression covered in Re-Ranking, removes noise before the model ever sees it.
This reduces the chance of an irrelevant chunk influencing the answer.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A post-retrieval filter that drops a low scoring chunk prevents that chunk from ever reaching the prompt, the same protective effect as top-k selection.

blocks.text: 5. Each Added Step Costs Latency
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719520-235685315.png
As with the cost and latency advantage covered in Naive RAG, every added pre or post retrieval step costs extra time and extra tokens.
The quality gain must be worth that added cost.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Pipeline","Relative cost"],"rows":[["Naive RAG","Lowest cost and latency"],["Advanced RAG with added steps","Higher cost, traded for higher quality"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Advanced RAG Is A Family Not A Single Technique

blocks.alt: Advanced RAG Is A Family Not A Single Technique
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719522-223915172.png
Modular RAG, corrective RAG, self-RAG, and adaptive RAG, covered next in this module, are all specific members of this same advanced RAG family.
Each one chooses a different specific correction to add.
7. Measuring Whether Added Steps Help
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719523-157708308.png
Without measuring the actual answer quality before and after adding a step, the added complexity is just a guess.
There is no way to confirm it actually helped.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Comparing answer quality on the same evaluation set before and after adding a correction step is the only way to know whether that specific step was worth its added cost.

blocks.text: 8. Incremental Adoption
Starting from naive RAG and adding one specific correction at a time keeps the pipeline debuggable.
This beats adopting every possible advanced technique all at once.
9. Recognizing When Advanced RAG Techniques Earn Their Added Cost

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Advanced RAG Techniques Earn Their Added Cost
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447719523-48936262.png
Naive RAG measurably failing on real queries justifies adding a specific correction.
Naive RAG already performing well, by contrast, does not need the added complexity.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates wrapping the naive pipeline with one pre-retrieval and one post-retrieval step.

code.content:
def rewrite_query(query):
    # improving the query before searching
    return query.strip().rstrip("?") + " pricing details"

def retrieve(query, chunks, top_k=3):
    return chunks[:top_k]

def filter_low_relevance(chunks, min_length=10):
    # improving the chunks before generating
    return [c for c in chunks if len(c) >= min_length]

def build_prompt(chunks, query):
    context = "\n".join(f"- {c}" for c in chunks)
    return f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {query}\nAnswer:"

chunks = [
    "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month.",
    "ok",
    "Refunds are processed within five business days.",
]
raw_query = "how much"

rewritten = rewrite_query(raw_query)
retrieved = retrieve(rewritten, chunks)
filtered = filter_low_relevance(retrieved)
prompt = build_prompt(filtered, raw_query)

print("Advanced RAG pipeline:")
print("Rewritten query:", rewritten)
print("Filtered chunks:", filtered)
print("Prompt:\n", prompt)

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the low value chunk being dropped by the post-retrieval filter before the prompt is built, the noise reduction from improving the chunks before generating.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Adding every possible advanced technique at once instead of one measured step at a time.
Confusing pre-retrieval query fixes with post-retrieval chunk fixes and applying the wrong one.
Skipping measurement, so there is no evidence an added step actually improved quality.
Applying advanced RAG complexity to a workload naive RAG already handles well.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Advanced RAG is the general shift toward inserting correction stages around the naive pipeline.
Pre-retrieval steps improve the query; post-retrieval steps improve the retrieved chunks.
Rewriting or expanding the query fixes the search itself rather than compensating later.
Re-ranking or filtering chunks removes noise before it ever reaches the model.
Every added step costs extra latency and tokens, so the quality gain must be worth it.
Modular RAG, corrective RAG, self-RAG, and adaptive RAG are all members of this same family.
Measuring quality before and after an added step is the only way to confirm it helped.
Incremental adoption, one correction at a time, keeps the pipeline debuggable.
Next up: Modular RAG, covering how these correction stages combine into swappable pipeline modules.
